newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait sheds Burgan Bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sheds Burgan Bank stake.

text.p: The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) has sold 130 million shares of its majority holdings in Burgan Bank in a public auction, officials said on Saturday.
The sale earned KIA, the state investment arm, 48.1 million dinars ($157.7 million), an investment official said.
The shares were sold to Kuwait Investment Projects Company (KIPCO) at the auction's starting price of 370 fils per share, he said. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
Burgan's share closed at 340 fils on Sturday.

KIA has announced plans to sell a total of 380 million of its 440 million Burgan Bank shares. Another 250 million shares will be put in public offering "soon", said an official. He did not give the price of the offering.
The 22-year-old bank's total subscribed shares amounted to 743.4 million shares at the end of 1996. The state's holdings in the bank make up some 59 percent of its issued shares.
Burgan had reported a net profit rise to 11.04 million dinars in 1996 compared to 8.05 million in 1995.

KIA, the state investment arm, has sold more than $2.5 billion worth of shares in local firms since the launch of a privatisation programme in 1994. It plans to sell shares worth about three billion dollars.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates -- can trade in Kuwaiti shares.
